profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap way, named "centro de datos trasbase Negratín" ("Negratín trans-basin data center" in Spanish), is located at the Negratín reservoir in Granada province, southern Spain. Negratín is part of Spain's inter-basin water transfer infrastructure, which moves water between river basins to support agriculture and municipal supply in water-scarce regions of southeastern Spain. Facilities described as a "centro de datos" at reservoir and water-transfer sites typically house SCADA (supervisory control and data acquisition) systems, telemetry equipment, and remote monitoring infrastructure used to track water levels, flow rates, and transfer operations across the network, a specialized industrial control application that is a fundamentally different use case from a commercial or enterprise data center hosting IT infrastructure for outside customers. This entry is filed as a likely water-infrastructure monitoring facility rather than a conventional data center, based on its name and location, without asserting fabricated IT capacity or building specifications that would not apply to a SCADA installation.
profile.research_note: This OSM way, named "centro de datos trasbase Negratín" (Spanish for "Negratín trans-basin data center"), sits at the Negratín reservoir in Granada province, Spain, a site associated with Spain's Tajo-Segura and related inter-basin water transfer infrastructure. "Centro de datos" here most plausibly describes a SCADA/telemetry data-acquisition hub monitoring water levels, flow, and transfer operations for the reservoir and transfer system, a specialized industrial control-and-monitoring installation, not a general-purpose commercial or enterprise IT data center.
